Chapter 10

Integration guide

Tokens, webhooks, embeds, feeds, the newsroom assistant connector and common integrations.

10.1  Choosing the right interface10.2  Public API10.3  Staff tokens10.4  Webhooks10.5  Feeds10.6  Embeds10.7  The newsroom assistant connector (MCP)10.8  Common integrations

This chapter shows how to connect Sham MediaOS to other systems: with API tokens, webhooks, feeds, embeds and the newsroom assistant connector. The complete list of operations is in the API reference later in this volume.

10.1Choosing the right interface

You want to… Use
Show the outlet's latest stories on another site RSS or JSON feeds, or the public API
Embed one story, an election result or a live page Embeds
Be told when a story is published or corrected Webhooks
Create or update stories from another system The newsroom API with a staff token
Let an AI assistant search and draft in the newsroom under a user's permissions The newsroom assistant connector (MCP)
Build reports The API, or read-only database access for reporting

10.2Public API

Public endpoints need no token: published stories, sections, topics, authors, editions, live pages, elections, podcasts and search. Always pass the edition's language code.

curl -s "https://api.horndaily.example/api/v1/articles?lang=en&limit=5" | jq '.data[].headline'

Responses use one envelope:

{"success": true, "data": [ ... ], "meta": {"next_cursor": "…", "language": "en", "direction": "ltr"}, "request_id": "01m6..."}

Errors:

{"success": false, "error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "That story does not exist in this edition.", "details": {}}, "request_id": "01m6..."}

10.3Staff tokens

Staff endpoints need a bearer token with the staff ability; sensitive endpoints also need a token issued after two-step verification (mfa). Tokens act with the permissions of the person they belong to, limited by their scopes.

To create a token for an integration

  1. Create a staff account for the integration (for example Wire importer) with only the role it needs.
  2. Sign in as that account and create a personal access token, or ask an administrator to issue one under Administration → Keys.
  3. Store the token in the other system's secret store. It is shown once.
  4. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.horndaily.example/api/v1/newsroom/articles \
  -d '{"language":"en","headline":"Rains return to the highlands"}'

Least privilege

Never use an administrator's token for an integration. Give the integration account the smallest role and scope, and an expiry date if it is temporary.

10.4Webhooks

Register an endpoint under Administration → Webhooks, choose the events and, optionally, the editions. Each delivery is a POST with a JSON body and these headers: X-JMN-Event (the event name), X-JMN-Delivery and X-JMN-Event-Id (identifiers for de-duplication), X-JMN-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-JMN-Signature, which is sha256= followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp, a dot and the raw body, keyed with the endpoint's secret.

import hmac, hashlib, time

def verify(secret: bytes, timestamp: str, body: bytes, signature: str) -> bool:
    if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 300:
        return False                      # too old: possible replay
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret, f"{timestamp}.".encode() + body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)   # signature = the X-JMN-Signature header

Deliveries are retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours. After 10 failures in a row the endpoint is switched off and administrators are told. Answer with a 2xx status quickly and do the work afterwards.

The events are listed in the Administrator Manual (Events, webhooks and languages) and in the developer portal at /developers/webhooks.

10.5Feeds

Every edition, section and topic has an RSS feed and a JSON feed. Podcasts have standard podcast feeds. News sitemaps are generated for search engines.

10.6Embeds

Stories, election results, contests and live pages can be embedded in other sites with an iframe from /embed/<lang>/…. Embeds respect the edition's language and direction and resize to fit.

10.7The newsroom assistant connector (MCP)

The newsroom exposes a Model Context Protocol server so that an AI assistant chosen by the outlet can search the archive, read wires and prepare drafts on behalf of a signed-in journalist, with that journalist's permissions only. It never publishes on its own, and investigation material is never available to it. It is off until an administrator switches it on.

10.8Common integrations

System How
Agency wires (AFP, Reuters, AP, regional agencies) Wire sources: RSS, Atom or agency feeds
Google News, search engines News sitemaps, structured data, feeds
Social platforms Social publishing and video upload with the outlet's own accounts
Telegram and WhatsApp channels Messaging channels
SMS gateways and USSD SMS provider settings
Payment providers Stripe, PayPal, Chapa, telebirr, ArifPay; bank transfer
E-mail SMTP or a transactional provider
Object storage and CDN S3-compatible storage; any CDN in front of the website
Single sign-on Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID, SAML 2.0
Vision mixers and streaming software Overlay pages as browser sources; stream destinations
Business intelligence API or a read-only database user for reporting

11.2obs-websocket v5 (bundled with OBS 28+)

  • Default port 4455. Messages {op, d}. Opcodes: 0 Hello, 1 Identify, 2 Identified, 3 Reidentify, 5 Event, 6 Request, 7 RequestResponse, 8 RequestBatch, 9 RequestBatchResponse.
  • Auth: secret = base64(sha256(password + salt)); authentication = base64(sha256(secret + challenge)). Test vector (obs-websocket protocol example; verified by the Studio Kit build and recomputed 19 October 2026): password supersecretpassword, salt lM1GncleQOaCu9lT1yeUZhFYnqhsLLP1G5lAGo3ixaI=, challenge +IxH4CnCiqpX1rM9scsNynZzbOe4KhDeYcTNS3PDaeY= → authentication 1Ct943GAT+6YQUUX47Ia/ncufilbe6+oD6lY+5kaCu4=.
  • eventSubscriptions: General 1, Config 2, Scenes 4, Inputs 8, Transitions 16, Filters 32, Outputs 64, SceneItems 128, MediaInputs 256, Vendors 512, Ui 1024, Canvases 2048 (5.7+). InputVolumeMeters = 65536 (explicit opt-in, every 50 ms).
  • Requests used by JMN: GetVersion, GetSceneList, SetCurrentProgramScene {sceneName}, SetCurrentPreviewScene, GetStudioModeEnabled, SetStudioModeEnabled, TriggerStudioModeTransition, GetStreamStatus, StartStream, StopStream, GetRecordStatus, StartRecord, StopRecord (→ outputPath), SetStreamServiceSettings {streamServiceType:"rtmp_custom", streamServiceSettings:{server,key}}, GetInputList, SetInputSettings {inputName, inputSettings:{url}} (browser_source), SetInputMute, GetInputMute, GetStats, CreateInput, GetSceneItemList, GetSceneItemId, SetSceneItemEnabled, PressInputPropertiesButton {propertyName:"refreshnocache"}.
  • Events: CurrentProgramSceneChanged {sceneName}, CurrentPreviewSceneChanged, StreamStateChanged {outputActive, outputState}, RecordStateChanged {outputActive, outputState, outputPath}, InputVolumeMeters {inputs[]}.
  • Browser security: ws://127.0.0.1 is not mixed content (loopback is potentially trustworthy). Chrome 147+ applies Local Network Access (loopback) permission prompts to WebSockets from public HTTPS sites — operators must allow "Apps on this device" once; managed fleets can pre-grant with the LocalNetworkAccessAllowedForUrls policy. The Studio Bridge avoids the prompt entirely (server-side relay).

11.3VDO.Ninja (AGPL-3.0, self-hostable static app + steveseguin/websocket_server)

  • Guest: ?room=ROOM&password=PW&push=ID&label=Name&quality=1&autostart
  • Director: ?director=ROOM&password=PW (&codirector for more)
  • OBS scene of the room: ?scene=0&room=ROOM&password=PW&cleanoutput (scene=1 director-curated)
  • One guest only: ?view=ID&solo&room=ROOM&password=PW&cleanoutput
  • Audio quality: &proaudio=1 on both push and view links. Bitrate (viewer): &videobitrate=2500.
  • Remote API: add &api=KEY; https://api.vdo.ninja/{KEY}/{action}/{target}/{value} or wss://api.vdo.ninja:443.

11.4Restream API

OAuth2 authorize https://api.restream.io/login?response_type=code&client_id=…&redirect_uri=…&state=…; token POST https://api.restream.io/oauth/token (form, client credentials via HTTP Basic; access 1 h, refresh 1 year, rotates). Scopes: profile.read channels.read channels.write stream.read. Endpoints (Bearer): GET /v2/user/profile, GET /v2/user/channels, GET /v2/user/streamKey (→ {streamKey, srtUrl}), GET /v2/user/ingest, GET /v2/server/all, GET /v2/user/events/upcoming, GET /v2/user/events/in-progress, chat URL GET /v2/user/webchat/url. Channel enable/disable: legacy PATCH /v2/user/channel/{id} {"active":bool} — UNVERIFIED, so the UI falls back to a deep link to the Restream dashboard when it fails. Default ingest rtmp://live.restream.io/live.

11.5StreamYard

No public API. Custom RTMP destinations need a paid plan. No documented RTMP input (bring OBS in through OBS Virtual Camera). MediaOS therefore stores StreamYard studio/guest links and, where the plan allows, a custom RTMP target that pushes into MediaOS's MediaMTX/YouTube destination.

11.6Icecast, BUTT, Mixxx

  • Icecast default port 8000, source user source. Status: /status-json.xsl (2.4; deprecated in 2.5) and /admin/publicstats.json (2.5, anonymous). In /status-json.xsl, icestats.source is an object for one mount and an array for several. /admin/publicstats.json is a top-level array ([{name:"icestats", ns}, {…, source}]) whose source is an object keyed by mount ({"/live": {…}}), with the title in display-title / metadata.x_icy_title (MediaOS's IcecastStatus parser handles all three shapes).
  • Metadata: GET /admin/metadata?mount=/live&mode=updinfo&song=Artist+-+Title (HTTP Basic).
  • BUTT: Icecast/SHOUTcast/WHIP; MP3, AAC+, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC; song from a text file; command-line remote control on port 1256 (-u "<song>", -s, -d, -S). The control port listens on the local machine only by default; never use -A (it opens the control port to every network interface, unauthenticated). The Bridge writes now-playing to the watched file.
  • Mixxx: Preferences → Live Broadcasting: Icecast 2, host, port 8000, mount /live, login source, password, MP3/Vorbis.

11.7MediaMTX 1.21

Ports: RTSP 8554, RTMP 1935, RTMPS 1936, HLS 8888, WebRTC 8889 (ICE UDP 8189), SRT 8890/UDP, API 9997 (off by default), metrics 9998. API GET /v3/paths/list → {itemCount, items:[{name, online, readers[], inboundBytes, tracks2[]}]}. OBS publish: RTMP rtmp://host/jmn-en · WHIP http://host:8889/jmn-en/whip · SRT srt://host:8890?streamid=publish:jmn-en. Recording keys: record, recordPath, recordFormat: fmp4, recordSegmentDuration, recordDeleteAfter. Publish auth: authMethod: internal with authInternalUsers per path.

11.8Platform ingest

YouTube rtmps://a.rtmps.youtube.com:443/live2 (backup rtmps://b.rtmps.youtube.com:443/live2?backup=1); embed https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/live_stream?channel=ID (behaviour UNVERIFIED — MediaOS prefers the per-event video ID). Facebook rtmps://rtmp-api.facebook.com:443/rtmp/ (prefer the API-provided secure_stream_url). X Live Studio and TikTok LIVE provide RTMP keys only to eligible accounts.

11.9Firebase Cloud Messaging HTTP v1

POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/messages:send, scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/firebase.messaging. Body {message:{topic|token, notification:{title,body,image}, data:{…}, android:{priority:"high", ttl:"3600s"}, apns:{headers:{"apns-priority":"10"}, payload:{aps:{sound:"default"}}}}}. The legacy API is shut down.

11.10Meld Studio and Meld Multi (owner request, 18 October 2026)

  • Meld Studio — free streaming/recording app for Windows and macOS (closed source; not part of the open-source default path). Multistreams natively to many destinations, runs a 16:9 and a 9:16 canvas together (Multi Canvas), unified chat. Meld Multi — Meld's cloud distribution (one upload, server-side fan-out), free in beta per the vendor. Source: https://meldstudio.co/blog/how-to-stream-to-multiple-platforms-at-once-without-plugins-or-relay-services/
  • Remote control API — Qt QWebChannel over WebSocket at ws://127.0.0.1:13376 (fixed port). Enable Settings → Advanced → Allow remote connections for LAN control. Object meld: properties isStreaming, isRecording, session.items (scenes, layers, tracks, effects keyed by 32-hex id), version; signals sessionChanged, isStreamingChanged, isRecordingChanged, gainUpdated; methods showScene, setStagedScene, showStagedScene, toggleLayer, toggleMute, toggleMonitor, setGain, toggleRecord, toggleStream, sendCommand('meld.startStreamingAction' | 'meld.stopStreamingAction' | 'meld.startRecordingAction' | 'meld.stopRecordingAction' | 'meld.toggleVirtualCameraAction' | 'meld.screenshot' | 'meld.recordClip'), setProperty(id, prop, value) (API v2). Source: https://github.com/MeldStudio/streamdeck/blob/main/WebChannelAPI.md
  • QWebChannel message types: 1 signal, 2 propertyUpdate, 3 init, 4 idle, 6 invokeMethod, 7 connectToSignal, 8 disconnect, 9 setProperty, 10 response. After each property-update batch the client sends {type:4}.
  • MediaOS mapping: the rundown scene map and studio commands are engine-neutral; the Studio Bridge and the Newsroom OS direct mode translate them for OBS (obs-websocket) or Meld (WebChannel). Stream-key configuration is OBS-only — Meld destinations and Meld Multi are managed inside Meld, and MediaOS records them as meld_multi destinations with watch/embed links.
Chapter 12

AI services

12.1  Models (commercial-safe only)12.2  Worker API (http://ai-worker:8090, bearer JMN_AI_WORKER_TOKEN)12.3  Governance (API side, AiWorkerGovernance)12.4  Features12.5  Production server checklist

Implements doc 33 items 9 (speech-to-text), 10 (translation memory, termbase, MT), 14 (semantic archive search) and 15 (verification toolkit). All inference runs on a private sidecar, services/ai-worker (Python 3.11, FastAPI). The Laravel API is its only client.

12.1Models (commercial-safe only)

Source: docs/research/notes/african_language_ai_models.md. Registry: services/ai-worker/models.yaml.

Model id Task Licence Download RAM (CPU int8) Languages
whisper-large-v3-turbo (deepdml CT2 build) STT MIT 1.6 GB ~2.2 GB ar, en, fr (+ other high-resource)
sunbird-whisper-51-african (Sunbird faster-whisper, gated: needs HF_TOKEN) STT Apache-2.0 3.1 GB ~3.8 GB am, om, so, sw
omnilingual-ctc-1b (Meta Omnilingual ASR) — disabled by default STT Apache-2.0 3.9 GB ~6 GB ti, sid, nus (+ am/om/so fallback)
madlad400-3b-mt (santhosh CT2 int8 conversion) MT Apache-2.0 3.0 GB ~4.2 GB am, om, so, ti, sw, ar, en, fr, aa
multilingual-e5-large (int8 ONNX from the repo) Embeddings (1024-d) MIT 0.6 GB ~1.2 GB all (no Tigrinya tag — evaluate)

Default set ≈ 9.3 GB on disk (+3.9 GB with Omnilingual), ~12 GB RAM when everything is loaded. Afar and Anuak have no commercial-safe STT model: routing is an explicit empty list and the worker answers 422.

Hard licence check (jmn_ai/registry.py): the worker refuses to start if any model's licence is not on the built-in allow-list (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, CC-BY-4.0, CC0, …) or its repo/upstream matches a non-commercial family (NLLB, MMS, SeamlessM4T, XTTS/Coqui, F5-TTS, Aya Expanse, afro-tts). The list is in code, not YAML. download.py re-runs the check, so a blocked model can never be fetched.

12.2Worker API (http://ai-worker:8090, bearer JMN_AI_WORKER_TOKEN)

Endpoint Purpose
GET /health liveness (no auth)
GET /status models, licences, installed/loaded state, download progress, routing, device, tools, free disk
POST /stt (multipart file, language, mode=sync\|async) timed segments, segment confidence = exp(avg_logprob), word confidence, has_speech (VAD)
POST /translate[?mode=async] sentence-segmented (Ge'ez ። ፧, Arabic ؟, Latin with abbreviations) MADLAD translation; preferred/do-not-translate terms inserted as constraints, forbidden terms and ignored constraints reported
POST /embed {texts, kind: query\|passage} L2-normalised e5 vectors with query:/passage: prefixes
POST /verify (multipart, mode) EXIF/XMP/IPTC/QuickTime (exiftool → Pillow/ffprobe fallback), C2PA (c2pa-python → JUMBF scan fallback), FFmpeg scene keyframes
GET /jobs/{id} async job status/result (kept 1 h; unknown → 404 → API resubmits)

Uploads go to a per-request temp dir and are deleted afterwards. Concurrency per task is bounded (JMN_AI_STT_CONCURRENCY …).

12.3Governance (API side, AiWorkerGovernance)

Same rules as AiAssistant (doc 10): ai.use in the output's scope; per-edition Pennant flag newsroom-ai (admin → Features or AI services); confidentiality gate — material linked to an uncleared investigation is never sent (only if the worker is on a private address and JMN_AI_WORKER_ALLOW_CONFIDENTIAL=true), refusals audited as ai.refused_confidential; every inference is an immutable ai_runs row (provider = jmn-ai-worker, new task transcription); output stays a draft until a person accepts/rejects it (ai_run_decisions). Embedding/indexing skips investigation-linked stories and search filters them out again. Metadata inspection is not AI and is not logged in ai_runs (it is audited by the fact-check desk).

Jobs: PollAiWorkerJob on queue ai submits to the worker then polls with back-off (each run is a short HTTP call, retryUntil 8 h), so no PHP worker holds a long request — the existing worker-low (low,ai,analytics) is enough. EmbedArticle (on ArticlePublished), IndexWireItems (scheduled every 5 min), PopulateTranslationMemory (on human approval/publication). Nothing is queued when JMN_AI_WORKER_URL is empty (TM population still runs — no AI).

12.4Features

  • Draft captions — captions desk (media page): "Draft captions with AI" → segments with time, confidence bar and low-confidence words highlighted; accept / edit / remove per segment, "accept confident (≥85 %)"; apply only when every segment is reviewed → new caption draft version (source asr) via MediaCaptions; publishing stays a human step. media_assets.speech_detected (detected or set by an editor).
  • Publish gate — StoryReadiness blocker captions_missing: video/audio with speech needs a published track in the edition's language. Per edition: languages.settings.captions_required (admin → AI services), default JMN_CAPTIONS_REQUIRED_DEFAULT=true.
  • TM + termbase + MT — tm_segments (pg_trgm GIN, exact = sha256 of normalised source, fuzzy ≥ 0.55); termbase_entries per edition (termbase.manage, granted to EIC, managing and senior editors; translators read); newsroom page /newsroom/termbase. Story inspector tab Translate: TM matches with %, termbase hits, forbidden terms found in the edition text, "Draft with TM + MT" (TM 100 % sentences reused, the rest to MADLAD with terms), per-sentence origin; "Use draft" saves the edition through ArticleService::saveTranslation with translation_source = machine_assisted (also upgrades an existing human row) → four-eyes approval and the public AI-use disclosure apply.
  • Semantic search — semantic_chunks (pgvector vector(1024) + HNSW when the extension is available, else real[]
  • exact jmn_dot() scan); stories list "Semantic (meaning)" mode (hybrid: 0.8 cosine + 0.15 headline match + 0.05 recency, same visibility as the story list); "Related coverage" in Story data; wires reading pane "Have we covered this?" (near-duplicate wires ≥ 0.88 across languages, stories ≥ 0.80). Backfill: php artisan jmn:ai:index.
  • Verification toolkit — fact-check page: private evidence upload (verification_files, private disk), original metadata summary + all fields, GPS → map / sun-position links, C2PA panel (valid / invalid / unverified / absent), keyframes; "Search this frame" (Google Lens, TinEye, Yandex, Bing) mints a 15-min signed URL to the metadata-free JPEG only on click (audited factcheck.frame_shared).
  • Admin → AI services (health.view/ai.manage): worker health, models + licences + state, STT routing, queue depth, 24 h outcomes, failures, per-edition switches.

12.5Production server checklist

  1. .env: JMN_AI_WORKER_URL=http://ai-worker:8090, JMN_AI_WORKER_TOKEN (generate-secrets.sh fills it), add ai to COMPOSE_PROFILES; optional HF_TOKEN of an account that accepted the Sunbird terms.
  2. pgvector: use pgvector/pgvector:pg17 (same data format as postgres:17) or install postgresql-17-pgvector, then as superuser CREATE EXTENSION vector; in the app DB before running the migrations (the app role is not a superuser). Without it the migration falls back to real[] (fine up to ~100k passages). To convert later: create the extension, ALTER TABLE semantic_chunks ALTER COLUMN embedding TYPE vector(1024) USING embedding::vector, then CREATE INDEX … USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops).
  3. Disk: ~10 GB in the ai-models volume (~14 GB with Omnilingual) + 4 GB tmpfs. First start downloads in the background; /status and the admin page show progress. Or bake: --build-arg JMN_AI_PRELOAD="multilingual-e5-large …".
  4. CPU (default): 4–8 vCPU, 12–16 GB RAM for the full set; STT at roughly 0.3–1× real time on 8 vCPU (Whisper turbo int8). GPU (recommended for backlogs / Omnilingual 7B): build with JMN_AI_BASE=nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu22.04, JMN_AI_DEVICE=cuda, add a compose override with deploy.resources.reservations.devices: [{capabilities: [gpu]}]; 24 GB VRAM (L4/A10/4090) fits the 7B Omnilingual LLM variant.

  5. php artisan migrate, then php artisan jmn:ai:index to embed the archive.

  6. Evaluate per language before enabling an edition (Amharic/Tigrinya WER ≈ 30–40 %): human caption QA and MT post-editing stay mandatory.

Chapter 13

API reference

This chapter lists every operation of the Sham MediaOS REST API version 1: 853 operations in 113 areas, generated from the OpenAPI document the server publishes at /api/v1/openapi.json. The same document drives the interactive reference in the developer portal (/developers/reference).

Conventions used in every endpoint

  • Base URL: https://api.your-domain/api/v1. All paths below are relative to it.
  • Every response is JSON in one envelope: {"success": true, "data": …, "meta": …, "request_id": "…"}; errors are {"success": false, "error": {"code", "message", "details"}}.
  • Public endpoints need no token. Staff endpoints need a bearer token with the staff ability; MFA marks endpoints that also need a token issued after two-step verification. Reader endpoints need a reader session.
  • Identifiers are 26-character lowercase ULIDs unless stated otherwise.
  • Rate limits are shown where a route sets its own; otherwise the area default applies (see the API specification chapter).

Chapter 14

Messages you may see

The system explains every refusal in plain words. This chapter collects 852 messages that the server can return, grouped by area, so that a help desk can search for the exact wording a user reports. The kind tells you the HTTP status family: Not allowed (403), Not found (404), Conflict (409), Check the form (422), Slow down (429), Unavailable (503).

The schema below was read from a freshly migrated Sham MediaOS 2.3.2 database: 266 tables grouped by business area. Columns show the PostgreSQL type; MySQL 8 and MariaDB installations use the equivalent types created by the same migrations.

Change data through the application

Write to these tables only through the application, its API or its commands. Direct writes bypass permissions, the audit chain, caches and search indexing. Use the tables for reporting and for read-only exports.

The Sham MediaOS library

Sham MediaOS is a newsroom, website, apps and broadcast platform that a news organisation installs on its own server, in its own languages, under its own brand. These volumes cover it from the reader's first visit to the engineer's last database migration.

01Product Bible — buyers, owners, managers and everyone new to the product
02Reader Guide — readers, help-desk staff and audience teams
03Newsroom User Manual — reporters, editors and newsroom staff
04Advanced User Manual — senior editors, producers, audience and commercial leads
05Administrator Manual — system administrators and technical owners
06Installation and Operations Manual — IT, hosting and operations staff
07Advanced Technical Manual — developers, integrators, architects and security reviewers
08Training Manual — trainers, new staff and team leads
09FAQ and Troubleshooting — everyone, and the help desk
10sham.et Store and Licensing Manual — customers buying licences and Sham operators
11Commercial and Legal Pack — buyers, procurement, legal and sales teams
